PullRequest.Title: Agent host chats: show a custom agent's argument-hint
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #349047

In agent host chats, a custom agent's `argument-hint` was not shown as the input placeholder:
- The agent host did not forward `argument-hint` with the agent, so the customization item had none. It now travels in the agent's `_meta` (`vscode.argumentHint`), like the model preferences.
- The session's generic placeholder ("Chat with Copilot") took precedence. The selected agent's hint is more specific, so it now wins, in the input editor decoration and in the widget's placeholder.

Split from #348918.

**Validation:** core typecheck; ChatWidget unit tests. Tested manually in Code OSS: the Agent Fix agent's chat shows "Explain the bug".

Scenarios.Scenario: Discover custom agents when an agent-host chat opens, and refresh after customization files change.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Customization readiness waits for discovery and publication. discoverAgents awaits the existing grouped SDK discovery request and then parses existing agent files serially; the diff only extracts and forwards argument-hint from those already-parsed files.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per discovery invocation, not one request per agent or root.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same grouped request ran before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before the agent-file parsing loop.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing read per eligible agent entry per discovery invocation; discoverAgents awaits these serially.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Every eligible file was already read and parsed for reasoning effort and model policy; argument-hint adds no read.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing serial reads gate the completed agent inventory.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve deduplicated discovery directories and ancestors, then reconcile filesystem watchers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One resolveAll call over a ResourceSet of directories and ancestors per discovery pass; watchers are reconciled rather than blindly accumulated.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical directory resolution, watch placement, and invalidation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs in the existing parallel discovery group.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Compare customization snapshots and publish session customization state carrying agent metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing snapshot publications now include at most one optional hint string per agent; unchanged discovered snapshots are rejected by equals in _refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same customization snapshots were compared and published without the hint field.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing state publication makes discovered hints available to clients.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N SDK-discovered, non-builtin agents with a path, grouped across the requested project roots; retained metadata grows with the sum of authored hint lengths.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The existing agent/rule/skill/hook/MCP discovery branches run in parallel; agent file parsing remains serial within its branch. Refresh requests use the existing 100 ms Delayer and cancellation; scheduling is unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Discovered directories are cached until relevant filesystem events invalidate them. SessionDiscoveredEntry retains the current customization snapshot and suppresses unchanged results. No new cache or key space is added.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed lines only add a frontmatter lookup and metadata field to an already-existing read/parse/publication path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Agent counts, file latency, and hint lengths vary, but none of the expensive call counts or scheduling policies increases.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Serial per-agent I/O is pre-existing, and forwarding an optional string does not establish a new expensive mechanism.

Scenarios.Scenario: Parse configured or synchronized agent plugins and construct protocol customizations.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Plugin resolution awaits format/manifest processing and parallel component readers. Agent enrichment waits for the existing markdown scan and file reads before returning parsed customizations.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve plugin component files and read each agent file for frontmatter enrichment.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing plugin format/manifest and component discovery operations, plus one parseAgentFile read per returned markdown file before final name deduplication.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same component discovery and file reads were performed; only the extracted argumentHint and optional _meta field are new.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Agent component directories and the effective discovered markdown files after readMarkdownComponents processing; frontmatter-name collisions are filtered after enrichment.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: parsePlugin reads component categories through Promise.all, and readAgentComponents uses Promise.all over discovered files. The diff changes neither parallelism nor read multiplicity.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: These parser functions add no cache. Existing caller refresh and plugin-resolution policies are unchanged; neither successful nor failed parsing gains a new retry path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: complete parser hunks and their callers show scalar metadata propagation without additional filesystem calls.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Plugin and file counts are installation-dependent; the additional work is a string lookup/trim and small metadata allocation per parsed agent.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Existing I/O fan-out is unchanged, and ordinary hint metadata allocation is not evidence of a performance bug.

Scenarios.Scenario: Populate an agent-host chat's custom-agent choices from session state.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: provideCustomAgents awaits the existing readiness gate and source-label resolution before mapping protocol agents to ICustomAgent objects. The new hint is read from existing metadata during that map.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Ensure the existing session-state subscription and await its first protocol snapshot when necessary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Shared subscription and memoized first-snapshot readiness per session subscription, not per agent.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same readiness wait and subscription sharing applied.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold callers wait; warm callers with an existing snapshot return immediately.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List extension prompt paths for source-label resolution through IPromptsService.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing listPromptFilesForStorage request per provideCustomAgents invocation, not per agent; downstream service caching is not altered by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same source-label lookup and agent/source mapping ran before the hint field was populated.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing awaited source-label preparation precedes mapping.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective session agents, or draft agents when the session inventory is empty; one optional hint per resulting agent.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Readiness and source resolution remain sequential stages of one provider request, followed by synchronous mapping. Hint lookup is in-memory.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Session snapshots and first-snapshot waits are already shared. The diff neither invalidates them nor introduces per-agent fetches, misses, or retry behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: provider and readiness implementation show no new remote or filesystem operation triggered by argumentHint.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Existing source-label service internals may cache results; no conclusion about their absolute cost is needed because invocation count is unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. This is metadata passthrough into an already-existing agent model and observable.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render chat input, change the selected custom agent or its hint, toggle sandbox mode, and dispose inline editing inputs.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The new autorun immediately applies the selected hint during input creation and on selected-mode/hint changes. Placeholder reconciliation and editor decoration updates run synchronously; normal typing uses the existing decoration path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One added autorun per created input, observing only the selected mode and that mode's hint; updates scale with mode/hint changes and active input count, not total discovered agents or transcript length.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: UI updates run on the renderer thread. The observer is registered in the existing widget or inline-edit DisposableStore; inline editing clears its store on teardown. Existing deferred decoration updates use a 200 ms ThrottledDelayer; the diff does not add per-keystroke subscriptions or asynchronous fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: ChatMode.updateData compares strings before changing the hint observable and batches property changes in a transaction. Sandbox reconciliation checks current versus desired placeholder before writing options. No new retained collection or cache is added.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced the autorun, placeholder setter, sandbox binding, mode observable updates, decoration listeners, and input disposal ownership.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Editor option updates can trigger existing rendering work, but the added updates occur at bounded mode/hint transitions; there is no evidence of a new loop, layout read/write cycle, or scaling reconstruction.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added observer is lifecycle-owned, and precedence changes select among already-supported placeholder strings without introducing a concrete expensive hot-path mechanism.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass across all eight changed files and every diff page against base 36e8c0289a5f29eae15a933263220d9895302ff6. Traced existing discovery I/O, plugin parsing, session publication/readiness, provider mapping, input rendering, observer updates, and disposal. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regressions or concrete performance-regression fixes were identified.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
